subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should OpenClaw require a full boundary-semantics fix for exact/near-`maxChars` paragraph breaks before landing this candidate, or accept the common-case text-only repair as partial?
rationale: The current text-only patch cannot preserve the separator in that boundary range while also respecting delivery limits, and there is a sibling PR for the same canonical issue.

options.title: Require full boundary preservation
options.body: Consolidate on one PR and carry paragraph seam semantics through an in-budget mechanism before merge.

options.title: Accept partial common-case repair
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally land the common paragraph case while leaving the overflow range tracked on the canonical issue.

options.title: Pause competing candidates
options.body: Keep one candidate open for owner direction and close or pause the duplicate implementation path.

recommendation.title: Require full boundary preservation
recommendation.body: Consolidate on one PR and carry paragraph seam semantics through an in-budget mechanism before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history points to paragraph-aware block streaming and newline streaming refinement in this area.
